golden_commit.success: Clean commit. Nobody opens the diff. We do not disturb miracles.
golden_commit.failure: Perfect commit missed. At least the TODO now has documented history.

open_source_contribution.success: PR merged. Strangers now know why this code should not be touched.
open_source_contribution.failure: PR closed. “Thanks!” is technically still feedback.

green_build.success: CI went green on the first try. The team agreed not to ask questions.
green_build.failure: Pipeline is red again. The log says yesterday was fine.

legacy_code.success: Refactor done. The new file is called legacy_adapter_final.js.
legacy_code.failure: Legacy stayed. It interpreted this as a contract extension.

deploy_friday.success: Deploy cancelled. Friday is a weekday again.
deploy_friday.failure: Deploy shipped. Chat went quiet: everyone is typing.

bug_production.success: Hotfix shipped. Prod works again; postmortem opened itself.
bug_production.failure: Bug stayed. The pager took that as an invitation to continue.

code_review.success: PR approved. The “small note” is now only 11 items.
code_review.failure: PR rejected. Author replied “got it.” Most alarming status today.

slack_huddle.success: Two-minute huddle. Twenty-three minutes later, a ticket exists.
slack_huddle.failure: Huddle declined. Context still arrived in six messages.

scope_creep.success: Focus saved. The “tiny change” moved to the next sprint.
scope_creep.failure: Change accepted. An hour later it had an epic and a roadmap.

slack_thread_storm.success: Status posted. The thread stayed calm for fourteen seconds.
slack_thread_storm.failure: Notifications muted. Came back to 68 messages and one “urgent.”

coffee_stain.success: Keyboard survived. Spacebar now requires respectful pressure.
coffee_stain.failure: Coffee stayed. The keyboard got liquid cooling without approval.

merge_conflict.success: Conflict resolved. Both branches believe they won.
merge_conflict.failure: Left for later. Later branched into two more branches.

canary_rollback.success: Canary rolled back. Errors fell; Friday is theoretically free again.
canary_rollback.failure: Waited a minute. Metrics waited too, then went up.

production_500_spike.success: Feature disabled. 500s vanished. Hypothesis temporarily unavailable.
production_500_spike.failure: Grafana refreshed. The spike is taller, but now it is real-time.

ci_pipeline_red.success: Logs read. It was the test that “never failed before.”
ci_pipeline_red.failure: Pressed Re-run. Failed faster. Pipeline values consistency.

friday_release_outage.success: Release rolled back. Prod is green. Friday still made the postmortem.

stack_overflow_down.success: Stack Overflow is back. Documentation may be closed again.
stack_overflow_down.failure: Stack Overflow is down. Documentation opened and stared first.

incidents.title: Certificate expires
incidents.body: The certificate expires in 11 minutes. Monitoring remembered before the calendar.

choices.label: Renew now
choices.risk: Lose momentum, close the incident immediately.

choices.label: Leave it till morning
choices.risk: Save time now, accept a visible penalty.

outcomes.punchline: Certificate renewed. The internet trusts you for another 90 days.
Certificate expired. The browser announced the release to clients first.

incidents.shareTemplate: Certificate: 11 minutes until production-grade calendar training.

incidents.title: Migration at 99%
incidents.body: The migration is stuck at 99%. The database waits for one query that is “almost done.”

outcomes.punchline: Lock cleared. 99% means almost done again.
A minute passed. Now 99% is the incident title.

incidents.title: Ghost feature flag
incidents.body: The feature has been off for three months. Seven percent of traffic disagrees.

choices.label: Freeze it OFF
choices.risk: Fast and safe, with almost no progress.

outcomes.punchline: Flag removed. Nobody knew why it existed — a promising sign.
Flag is permanently off. The code still checks it anyway.

incidents.shareTemplate: Feature disabled. The code has not received the memo.

incidents.title: Queue backlog
incidents.body: The queue grows faster than workers can pretend everything is normal.

choices.label: Raise timeout
choices.risk: The queue gets quieter; progress barely changes.

outcomes.punchline: Queue drained. The chart looks like a chart, not career growth.
Timeout raised. The system now fails more slowly and confidently.

incidents.shareTemplate: Queue growing. Workers maintain a professional expression.

incidents.title: Flaky test
incidents.body: One test turns red every fifth build. The team already knows it by name.

choices.label: Quarantine and fix
choices.risk: Spend time now for a stable CI later.

choices.label: Re-run until green
choices.risk: Fast, stressful, and not actually fixed.

outcomes.punchline: Flaky test fixed. Pipeline has stopped running a lottery.
Green on the fourth Re-run. Cause officially undetermined.

incidents.shareTemplate: CI is green. The method is not part of the report.

incidents.title: Cache stampede
incidents.body: The cache expired all at once. Backend met all traffic personally.

choices.label: Raise limits
choices.risk: Fast symptom relief paid in resources and nerves.

outcomes.punchline: TTLs spread out. The next panic is at least distributed.
Limits raised. The server got more resources for the same mistake.

incidents.shareTemplate: Cache expired together. Architecture values teamwork.

incidents.title: On-call handoff
incidents.body: The shift is over. The runbook ends with: “if needed, ask the on-call engineer.”

choices.label: Update the runbook
choices.risk: Spend energy on docs instead of current pace.

choices.label: Hand it over verbally
choices.risk: Fast, but context becomes oral tradition.

outcomes.punchline: Runbook updated. The on-call engineer is a person again, not a dependency.
Handoff was verbal. An hour later, only the word “there” remained.

incidents.shareTemplate: On-call handed over. Context currently exists in oral form.

incidents.title: Major update
incidents.body: A library offers a major update. The changelog has 38 breaking changes and the word “simple.”

choices.label: Upgrade now
choices.risk: High load now for substantial technical progress.

outcomes.punchline: Upgrade survived. Breaking changes ended at item 41.
Version pinned. The future has officially moved to backlog.

incidents.shareTemplate: Major update: simple. Changelog: 38 reasons to redefine simple.
